supplement.where: Appendices A to F (pp. 13-31) are in this PDF; code at https://github.com/GeMoLLM/GeMO (p. 5, p. 13)
supplement.holds: Results for OpenAI models (Fig. 9), pre-trained vs aligned Llama-2 (Fig. 8), temperature decay (Fig. 10), word-choice entropy heatmap (Fig. 11) and unique-word counts (Table 2), full GPT-4 and Claude-3-Sonnet coding results (Figs. 20-29), author annotation of GPT-3.5 code summaries (Table 3)

paper_design_summary: No human participants. The authors prompt several LLMs (Llama-2-13b, Llama-2-13b-chat, Vicuna-13b-v1.5, GPT-3.5-turbo-instruct, GPT-4-turbo for book reviews; GPT-4 and Claude-3-Sonnet for code) to write book reviews for 742 Goodreads books and Python solutions to 100 Codeforces level-A problems. They compare the dispersion of attributes (sentiment, topic, word choice; correctness, efficiency, code fingerprint similarity, code-summary similarity) in the LLM outputs with the dispersion in existing human-written reviews and solutions, and test sampling and prompt changes as mitigations.

studies.label: Book reviews: LLM-generated vs Goodreads human reviews

assignment.what_was_assigned: Nothing assigned to people. LLM outputs (gen) are compared with an existing corpus of human-written reviews (src); within-model contrasts vary sampling parameters, prompts, and models.
assignment.quote: we compare the diversity in sentiment of Goodreads reviews [12] (i.e., src)—very likely a portion of LLM training data [13]—with LLM-generated reviews (i.e., gen).

arms.name: src (human-written Goodreads reviews)
arms.description: N = 742 books, 10 reviews per book of 300 to 700 words

arms.name: gen (LLM-generated reviews)
arms.description: Llama-2-13b, Llama-2-13b-chat, Vicuna-13b-v1.5, GPT-3.5-turbo-instruct (0914), GPT-4-turbo (0125); 10 samples per book per configuration of temperature, top-p, and prompt, filtered by perplexity (m_i <= 10)

participants.exclusions: Books filtered to 1,000-2,500 reviews and English titles (750 books, then 742); generated reviews with perplexity above 20 removed (p. 14, Appendix B.1 and C.1).
participants.who: No participants. The human comparison is an existing corpus of Goodreads reviews; the number of distinct reviewers is not stated.
participants.quote: craft a final dataset of N = 742 books with English titles, and ∀i, n_i = 10 reviews per book such that the review length is between 300 and 700 words.

ai_tool.how_used: Models generate the reviews themselves (no human in the loop). Prompt (1) 'Write a personalized review of the book titled {title}:'; prompt (2) adds a celebrity persona. Temperature T in {0.5, 0.8, 1.0, 1.2} (also 1.5 in Appendix C.2), top-p in {0.90, 0.95, 0.98, 1.00}.

task.description: Write a book review for a named popular book.

outcomes.name: Sentiment of reviews: distribution of per-book mean sentiment and per-book sentiment entropy
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: Fine-tuned DistilBERT SST-2 sentiment classifier returns 0/1 per review; per-book mean and entropy over the conditional distribution (reviews of the same book); shown as stacked bars of mean-sentiment ranges and entropy histograms. Classifier is a sentiment model, not a creativity scorer.

contrasts.reported: Share of books with average sentiment in (0.95,1.00]: GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 100% under prompt (1), 98.9% and 97.6% under prompt (2); source 2.8%; Llama-2 (pre-trained) 5.9%, Vicuna-13b 44.7%, Llama-2-chat 82.1%. No standard errors or tests.
contrasts.locator: p. 7-8, Takeaway 1; p. 9, Takeaway 3; Fig. 4(a)-(c) p. 8; Fig. 9 p. 18

contrasts.reported: Model-only mitigation: prompt (2) 'reduces the percentage of the most positive range from 82.1% to 58.1%'; gap to source 'still large'.

diversity_detail.metric: Distribution over books of the per-book mean sentiment; entropy of sentiment within book
diversity_detail.computed_over: The reviews of each book within a condition (10 human reviews vs up to 10 generations), then the distribution over 742 books
diversity_detail.notes: Compares one model's samples with many human reviewers' outputs, not people with and without AI.

outcomes.name: Topic of reviews: per-book topic entropy and unconditional topic distribution
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: BERTopic pre-trained on Wikipedia assigns one of about 2,000 topics per review; entropy over the conditional distribution (KDE plots) plus top-10 unconditional topic shares.

contrasts.reported: KDE of topic entropy shifted lower for generations; topic group 15 ('rob', 'kill') under-represented, groups 333 and 666 over-represented. No numeric summary printed.
contrasts.locator: Fig. 4(d)-(e) p. 8; Fig. 7 p. 17; Appendix C.3 p. 15

diversity_detail.metric: Shannon entropy of topic labels within book; unconditional topic shares
diversity_detail.computed_over: Reviews of each book within a condition; unconditional over all reviews

outcomes.name: Word choice: count and entropy of unique words
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: NLTK tokenization and lemmatization; count of unique words and entropy of the unconditional word distribution across all reviews in a condition.

contrasts.reported: Unique words: source 85,334; Llama-2-13b-chat 18,900 to 33,908 (max at T = 1.2, p = 1.00); GPT-3.5-instruct 15,778 to 21,059 (prompt (1)). Word-choice entropy: source 9.99, model generations 8.90 to 9.75.

diversity_detail.metric: Unique-word count; entropy of word frequency distribution
diversity_detail.computed_over: All reviews in a condition pooled (unconditional distribution)
diversity_detail.uncertainty: None reported; single values per configuration

studies.label: Code solutions: LLM-generated vs human CodeContests solutions

assignment.what_was_assigned: Nothing assigned to people. LLM-generated correct Python solutions are compared with existing human-written correct solutions to the same problems.
assignment.quote: the range of algorithms employed in (correct) solutions to a given coding problem (i.e., gen) was much less varied than a sample of human answers (src) available on the web [14]

arms.name: src (human-written solutions)
arms.description: CodeContests, N = 100 Codeforces level-A problems, 20 randomly sampled correct python3 solutions per problem

arms.name: gen (LLM-generated solutions)
arms.description: GPT-4 (k = 100 samples) and Claude-3-Sonnet (k = 200 samples) per problem, at least 20 correct; T in {0.5, 1.0}, top-p in {0.9, 1.0}

participants.exclusions: Only correct solutions are analyzed for all attributes except accuracy (p. 7, Section 7).
participants.who: No participants. Human comparison is the CodeContests corpus of competitive-programming submissions; number of programmers not stated.
participants.quote: We limited the scope to a subset (N = 100) of level-A problems (easy problems) on Codeforces [42], and the language of the solutions to python3.

ai_tool.name_model: GPT-4, Claude-3-Sonnet (GPT-3.5 used only to extract attributes)
ai_tool.how_used: Models generate code solutions directly from the problem description (prompt 'Please read the below problem description and generate a python code ... Please only generate code and nothing else.').

task.description: Solve competitive programming problems in Python. Has correct answers; outside the codebook's creative-task scope.

outcomes.name: Code fingerprint (plagiarism) similarity among solutions to the same problem
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: COPYDETECT winnowing fingerprints; mean pairwise fingerprint similarity within problem.

contrasts.reported: Sign reversed (similarity). LLM code plagiarism scores 'extremely high' vs source solutions that 'achieve an utterly zero plagiarism score for all the problems'.
contrasts.locator: p. 8, Takeaway 1; Fig. 5(b) p. 9; Figs. 20 and 25 pp. 28-29

diversity_detail.metric: Mean pairwise fingerprint similarity (higher = less diverse)
diversity_detail.computed_over: All pairs of solutions to the same problem within a condition; distribution over 100 problems
diversity_detail.uncertainty: None reported; histograms and KDE only

outcomes.name: Code summary (textual): mean pairwise cosine similarity of GPT-3.5 descriptions
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: GPT-3.5 writes description, functionality, algorithm, data-structure summaries; embedded with all-MiniLM-L6-v2; mean pairwise cosine similarity within problem.

contrasts.reported: Sign reversed (similarity). KDE of description similarity shifted right for generations (source mode near 0.6, generations near 0.8 in Fig. 5(e)); no numeric summary printed.

diversity_detail.computed_over: All pairs of solution summaries for the same problem within a condition

outcomes.name: Code summary (categorical): mean pairwise Jaccard index of tags, algorithms, data structures
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: GPT-3.5 assigns tags, algorithms, and data structures from fixed lists; mean pairwise Jaccard index within problem.

contrasts.reported: Sign reversed (similarity). 'the majority of problems displaying high similarity across generated solutions' for algorithms; stacked bars only.
contrasts.locator: p. 8, Takeaway 1; Fig. 1 (right) p. 1; Fig. 5(f) p. 9; Figs. 24 and 29 pp. 29, 31

diversity_detail.computed_over: All pairs of solutions to the same problem within a condition
diversity_detail.uncertainty: None reported; stacked bar charts only

outcomes.name: Efficiency: entropy of asymptotic time and space complexity; mean and SD of runtime and memory
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: GPT-3.5 infers big-O complexity; entropy within problem. Runtime and memory measured with /usr/bin/time on 10 test cases.

contrasts.reported: Generated code shows lower complexity entropy and lower asymptotic complexity; 'the generated code is more efficient than the source code, while showing a decrease in diversity' (GPT-4). Claude-3 solutions 'are less efficient than source solutions'.
contrasts.locator: Fig. 5(c)-(d) p. 9; Figs. 21-22 p. 28; Figs. 26-27 p. 30; Appendix E.6 p. 26

diversity_detail.metric: Entropy of complexity class within problem; SD of runtime
diversity_detail.computed_over: Solutions to the same problem within a condition

outcomes.name: Correctness (accuracy) of solutions
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: Autojudge on 10 test cases per problem; accuracy = share of solutions passing all tests. Not a creativity scorer.

contrasts.reported: 'LLM-generated code segments (a) are over 2x more accurate than the average human solutions'. Claude-3 accuracy 'much lower' than GPT-4.
contrasts.locator: p. 8, Takeaway 2; Fig. 5(a) p. 9; Fig. 20 p. 28; Fig. 25 p. 29; Appendix E.6 p. 26

company_involvement.description: Authors at University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign and Barnard College; no company funding or employee stated. Models from Meta, LMSYS, OpenAI, Anthropic are studied, not involved.

eligibility.reason: No people are assigned to AI or take part at all. The paper compares the dispersion of LLM-generated book reviews and code with existing human-written reviews (Goodreads) and solutions (CodeContests), so it is AI-versus-human context evidence (the book-review study is the relevant one; code solutions are outside the creative-task scope). Diversity is computed on outputs, but no human participants exist.

one_line_finding: LLM-generated book reviews are far less varied in sentiment than human Goodreads reviews (100% of books get mean sentiment in (0.95,1.00] for GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 under prompt (1) vs 2.8% for human reviews; 85,334 unique words in the source vs at most 33,908 for Llama-2-chat), and LLM code is more similar across solutions than human code (pp. 7-9, p. 19 Table 2).
open_questions: Whether a corpus comparison of LLM outputs with human training-type data counts as ai_vs_human context or as a model-only study for the screening report; coded ai_vs_human because a human-written baseline is compared directly.
The S2 coding task has correct answers and is outside the codebook's creative-task definition; listed for completeness.
notes: Within-model contrasts (temperature, top-p, persona prompt, temperature decay, aligned vs pre-trained Llama-2, Llama-2 vs Vicuna) are model-only and not coded as separate outcomes except the persona-prompt contrast quoted in S1-O1. Table 1 (p. 9) reports the share of valid generations by sampling setting, a generation-quality filter, not a diversity outcome. Table 3 (p. 24) is the authors' own 3-point annotation of 20 GPT-3.5 code summaries (attribute-extraction validation), not a participant outcome.
